declarations.description: An item's scope for the toolkit's tools, in a section player's card or around a host's own item player. A host gives it the item, its `item-id` and its policy `settings`; the toolbars and tools inside take the item from it and act on it, and it registers the item with the enclosing `<pie-assessment-toolkit>`, which files the item's accessibility catalogs. In a toolkit that holds a section it is also the item's channel to that toolkit; otherwise the item player's events pass through unchanged.
declarations.name: ItemScope

events.description: Registration handshake, once a toolkit has answered the scope and again when the item's identity, settings or catalogs change; the toolkit whose `runtimeId` it carries claims it and stops its propagation.

declarations.description: The toolbar for an item, passage or section, rendering a button for each tool the enclosing toolkit's coordinator places at its `level` and the tool's own visibility and applicability checks keep, plus the host's own `hostButtons`. It takes the item and its id from the enclosing `<pie-item-scope>` and the tool registry from the toolkit, either of which a host can override on the toolbar. Its tools act on the scope, or on the element `scopeElement` names.
declarations.name: ItemToolBar

declarations.description: The toolkit's runtime element: it holds a `ToolkitCoordinator` and provides its tools, policy and services to the toolbars, item scopes and item players inside it, with or without a bound section. A host gives it tool configuration, an `assessment` carrying the personal needs profile, and optionally a `section` to bind, its own `coordinator` or a `toolRegistry`. It builds its coordinator from those inputs unless one is passed or an outer toolkit's is inherited.

members.description: Interface locale, published onto the runtime context so every tool resolves the same provider. `type: "String"` because hosts pass attribute values as strings and a BCP-47 tag is one; POSIX (`nl_NL`) and bare (`nl`) forms both resolve.

cssProperties.name: --pie-annotation-underline
cssProperties.description: Colour of the student annotation underline on a light page, default #4221d5. Deliberately does not fall through --pie-primary: a theme accent is chosen against one background and is illegible on the other, and a var() fallback could never override a host-set --pie-primary anyway. Paired with --pie-annotation-underline-dark, which HighlightCoordinator selects via [data-theme] rather than prefers-color-scheme. The data-color-scheme accessibility palettes set both to their own --pie-primary, because [data-theme] reports what the page declares rather than which scheme is active. Hosts overriding it must keep 3:1 against the content background (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11).

cssProperties.name: --pie-annotation-underline-dark
cssProperties.description: Colour of the student annotation underline on a dark page, default #9c89ec. The dark half of the pair described under --pie-annotation-underline; kept a separate token so overriding one state never silently moves the other. Hosts overriding it must keep 3:1 against the content background (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11).

cssProperties.name: --pie-tts-line-highlight
cssProperties.description: Line-granularity reading highlight. HighlightCoordinator derives a value from the resolved theme and writes it inline on the document element, so a host declaration wins only with !important. Falls back through --pie-tts-sentence-highlight, then --pie-missing at 38%.

cssProperties.name: --pie-tts-sentence-highlight
cssProperties.description: Sentence-granularity reading highlight, and the fallback for --pie-tts-line-highlight. HighlightCoordinator derives a value from the resolved theme and writes it inline on the document element, so a host declaration wins only with !important. Falls back to --pie-missing at 38%.

cssProperties.name: --pie-tts-word-highlight
cssProperties.description: Current-word reading highlight. HighlightCoordinator derives a value from the resolved theme and writes it inline on the document element, so a host declaration wins only with !important. Falls back to --pie-missing at 68%.

cssProperties.name: --pie-tts-word-shadow
cssProperties.description: Text shadow carrying the current word over a saturated highlight. HighlightCoordinator derives a value from the resolved theme and writes it inline on the document element, so a host declaration wins only with !important. Falls back to --pie-text at 35%.

cssProperties.name: --pie-tts-word-underline
cssProperties.description: Underline on the current word, the non-colour cue for schemes where the highlight hue washes out. HighlightCoordinator derives a value from the resolved theme and writes it inline on the document element, so a host declaration wins only with !important. Falls back to --pie-text at 70%.

declarations.description: A section-level toolbar: a `<pie-item-toolbar>` at level `section`, scoped to the section a host names in `section-id`, rendering the tools in `enabled-tools` plus any `hostButtons`. The enclosing toolkit's coordinator drives the personal needs profile inputs through its policy engine, so the toolbar resolves none of them itself.
declarations.name: SectionToolBar
